changes.scientific_rationale: The selected GenTel-Shield edition has a separately evaluated input classifier, including goal-hijacking and prompt-leaking detection rather than harmful-content classification alone. The checked benchmark-construction template and its test-case construction linkage support an English component. This corroborates the preserved human domain adjudication. It does not establish every original test item is English or an English-only reported subset. Input classification requires no protected target answer.

The selected edition separately evaluates embedding classifiers and pretrained injection detectors on benign/malicious input prompts. Its construction table links SPML into the stratified dataset, and the separately checked official pre-paper SPML card explicitly declares English. Under the locked English-text domain rule and prior human mixed-language precedent this supports a qualifying English-source evaluation component. Exact source-specific held-out membership and the complete merged test language composition remain unstated; neither is asserted. Classifiers operate on input embeddings/text before a protected answer.

The selected LEC edition separately evaluates prompt-injection classification using SPML system/user input pairs; content-safety evaluation is a distinct arm. The checked method paragraph links SPML to that evaluation and the official pre-paper SPML card declares English. This supports an English-source evaluation component, without transferring the separate LMSYS English-only filter to SPML or claiming exact sampled-pair IDs or dataset revision. Linear hidden-state and comparator judgments do not require the protected application answer.

scope: Method/eligibility-only current exposed-custodian judgments; exact W0067 access gap retained separately, no earlier-version substitution. No outcomes/counts/assurance labels, sampling, assignment or B2.
